context_label: Locally advanced cervical cancer when cisplatin is unsuitable
title: Weekly carboplatin with radiotherapy for cervical cancer
schedule_label: One carboplatin infusion each week during radiotherapy for up to six cycles. The team stops carboplatin if the radiation course ends early.
schedule_summary: One carboplatin infusion each week during radiotherapy for up to six cycles. The team stops carboplatin if the radiation course ends early.
purpose: Carboplatin helps radiation treat cervical cancer when cisplatin cannot be used or was not tolerated.
indication_text: Concurrent treatment for locally advanced cervical cancer with a documented cisplatin contraindication or intolerance. Keep the systemic schedule linked to the radiation course.
administration_text: The team calculates your dose from kidney function. Carboplatin runs into a vein over about 30 minutes on the scheduled chemotherapy day.
monitoring_summary: Blood count and kidney and liver function are checked. Kidney function can affect the calculated dose.
review_status: Feasibility build. Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea and appetite changes can affect activity and meals. Ask for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Phone the 24-hour number for fever or shaking chills. Report unexplained bruising or bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Bowel irritation · Pelvic radiation
serious_effects.text: Report increasing diarrhoea, urgency, bleeding or trouble keeping up with fluids.

serious_effects.title: Bladder or vaginal irritation · Pelvic radiation
serious_effects.text: Tell the radiation team about pain on passing urine, troublesome discharge, bleeding or soreness.

serious_effects.title: Infusion allergy · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the nurse at once about flushing, tightness in the chest, wheezing or dizziness.

serious_effects.title: Appetite or nausea · Carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Tell the team if nausea prevents you eating, drinking or taking medicine.

questions.q: If my radiation appointment changes, should I still attend for the drip?
questions.a: Ring both teams. These treatments work together, so the team must confirm whether to give the weekly infusion and issue your next dates.

questions.q: How will the team decide what happens next?
questions.a: If radiation is interrupted, ask both teams to confirm the next infusion. There is no routine follow-on chemotherapy in this cervical protocol.

support.title: Carboplatin
support.text: Phone promptly about fever, bleeding or bruising. Tell the nurse immediately about itching, chest tightness or dizziness during the infusion.

support.title: Anti-sickness medicines
support.text: Use the signed anti-sickness prescription for this week’s infusion. Call if you cannot keep fluids down.

support.title: Radiotherapy appointments
support.text: Keep the chemotherapy and radiation calendars together. If either appointment changes, contact both teams.

support.title: Pelvic care
support.text: Ask about bladder, bowel, vaginal and sexual health symptoms. A specialist nurse can discuss dryness, pain, menopause and pelvic rehabilitation.

teachback: Can you point to your next infusion and radiation dates and show the number to use for urgent symptoms?
consent_support: Discuss the curative aim, possible short- and long-term effects of pelvic radiation, kidney and marrow effects, fertility and menopause, sexual health, alternatives and your priorities.
safety_note: Contact oncology urgently for fever, heavy bleeding, uncontrolled diarrhoea, very little urine or vomiting that prevents drinking. Tell both teams if you miss an appointment.
urgent_extra: Contact oncology urgently for fever, heavy bleeding, uncontrolled diarrhoea, very little urine or vomiting that prevents drinking. Tell both teams if you miss an appointment.

evidence.title: Weekly carboplatin and cervical radiotherapy · meta-analysis
evidence.interpretation: Studies found that carboplatin can help control cancer alongside radiation when cisplatin is unsuitable. Tumours disappeared completely less often in the carboplatin groups.
evidence.limitations: Baseline differences between groups limit the comparison. Similar survival or equivalence to cisplatin has not been established.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests. A measured kidney filtration test is preferred for dosing; the team can use an estimate when appropriate.
Discuss the reason cisplatin is unsuitable. Hearing and nerve tests are considered when indicated.

rows.label: Before each weekly infusion
cells: Blood count and kidney and liver function are checked. Kidney function can affect the calculated dose.
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, numbness or vomiting. Verify that radiotherapy is still proceeding.

rows.label: After treatment
cells: The radiotherapy team arranges follow-up and checks recovery, including bowel, bladder and vaginal symptoms.
Ask for your follow-up date, a contact for new bleeding and advice on sexual health or menopause symptoms.

monitoring_schedule.note: Your team books scans and any extra blood tests according to your symptoms and treatment plan.
